products.name: Dynook
products.description: Dynook turns the notch on your MacBook into a quiet home for what's happening right now. Timers, music, calls and meetings appear beside the camera while they're live, then tuck away. Click the notch for a frosted-glass panel of handy tools.
products.platform: macOS 14 Sonoma or later. Made for MacBooks with a notch; on other Macs it sits at the top of the screen as a small pill.
features: Timers, stopwatch and Focus sessions with a countdown beside the notch
Now Playing for Apple Music and Spotify, glowing in the colours of the album art
Meeting heads-up with one-click Join for Zoom, Meet, Teams, Webex and FaceTime
Shelf: drop files on the notch, then drag them out, AirDrop, zip or merge them
Clipboard history, quick notes, calendar and reminders a click away
Works with Shortcuts, and no account, ads or analytics

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body: Dynook doesn't collect any personal data. There's no account, no analytics, no ads and no tracking, and nothing you do in Dynook is sent to me.

sections.heading: What stays on your Mac
sections.body:
Your notes, clipboard history, Shelf files, saved Pomodoro timers, Shortcut widgets and settings are stored only on your Mac, inside Dynook's own storage. They're never uploaded anywhere. Deleting Dynook removes them.

In Dynook Direct, Claude Code permission prompts travel over a private connection on your Mac only.

sections.heading: Permissions
sections.body:
Dynook asks for each permission only when you first use the feature that needs it, and every other feature keeps working if you say no.

- **Calendars and Reminders**: to show your next event, meeting heads-ups and today's reminders. Read on your Mac only.
- **Spotify and Music**: to show what's playing and to play, pause and skip. Dynook only talks to them while they're already open.
- **Files you drop or choose, and your Downloads folder**: for the Shelf and download alerts.
- **Clipboard**: for clipboard history, which is off until you turn it on. Items that apps mark as private, such as passwords, are skipped.
- **Bluetooth**: to show the battery of your connected AirPods, mice and keyboards on the Battery card. Dynook only listens while that card is open, reads the battery levels on your Mac, and doesn't keep or send them.
- **Microphone**: Dynook only checks *whether* an app is using the microphone, to show calls. It never records or listens.

sections.heading: Shortcuts
sections.body: Dynook's Shortcuts actions (live activities, notch alerts and Shortcut widgets) run on your Mac. Whatever your shortcuts show in Dynook stays on your Mac. If a widget asks to be refreshed, Dynook only runs the shortcut you named; anything that shortcut does online is done by the shortcut, not Dynook. A link in a widget opens only when you click it.

sections.heading: When Dynook goes online
sections.body:
Only to fetch album art for the song that's playing:

- **Spotify**: the track's ID is sent to open.spotify.com.
- **Apple Music**: for songs without their own artwork, the song title and artist are sent to Apple's iTunes Search (itunes.apple.com).

As with any web request, those services also see your IP address. Their own privacy policies apply. Nothing is sent to me, and nothing else leaves your Mac.

sections.heading: Children
sections.body: Dynook doesn't collect personal data from anyone, including children.

sections.heading: Changes
sections.body: If this policy changes, the updated version will be on this page with a new date.

sections.heading: Contact
sections.body: Questions about privacy or Dynook? Reach me through the [contact page](/contact).
